title: The compiler was supposed to end programming too
title_zh: 编译器本来也 supposed 要终结编程的

paragraphs.en: In 1954, IBM said FORTRAN would virtually eliminate coding and debugging. What the numbers say about AI and software work in 2026, and my guess at a developer's Tuesday in 2031.
paragraphs.zh: 1954年，IBM曾表示FORTRAN将几乎消除编码和调试工作。 关于2026年人工智能与软件工作，数字说明了什么，以及我对2031年一名开发者某个周二的猜测。

paragraphs.en: The agent could write refund code all day long. What it can’t do is decide what your company owes a customer whose card has expired, so it stopped and asked, which is exactly what you’d want from a new hire too. Your morning goes like this: you read three pull requests, you go and talk to someone in support, and you write the rule down so clearly that nobody (human or otherwise) has to guess again.
paragraphs.zh: 这个智能体可以一整天都在写退款代码。 它做不到的是决定你的公司欠一位信用卡已过期的客户多少钱，所以它停下来询问了，而这正是你对一个新员工同样期待的。 你的早晨是这样的：你阅读三个拉取请求，去和客服支持的人交谈，然后把规则写得清清楚楚，以至于没有人（无论人类还是其他）需要再猜测。

paragraphs.en: I made that Tuesday up. None of it is science fiction, though. Agents that work unattended overnight exist today, and one of them runs on my own machine every night at ten. It invents a small project, builds it, tests it, and I find out what it made over breakfast. The first morning, I had no idea what it had built. That build is now Rule Safari , a live project on this site, with an article explaining how it works.

paragraphs.en: On 10 November 1954, IBM’s Programming Research Group finished a preliminary report on a new language called FORTRAN. One sentence in it says that FORTRAN “should virtually eliminate coding and debugging.”
paragraphs.zh: 1954年11月10日，IBM的编程研究小组完成了一份关于一种名为FORTRAN的新语言的初步报告。 报告中有一句话写道，FORTRAN“应当能几乎消除编码和调试工作”。

sents.en: On 10 November 1954, IBM’s Programming Research Group finished a preliminary report on a new language called FORTRAN.
sents.zh: 1954年11月10日，IBM的编程研究小组完成了一份关于一种名为FORTRAN的新语言的初步报告。

sents.en: One sentence in it says that FORTRAN “should virtually eliminate coding and debugging.”
sents.zh: 报告中有一句话写道，FORTRAN“应当能几乎消除编码和调试工作”。

paragraphs.en: I love this sentence. It’s so sure of itself, and it even came with a budget: problems solved “for less than half the cost” of doing it without FORTRAN. The industry had a name for this kind of thing back then. Assemblers and compilers were called automatic programming . You’d describe what you wanted, and the machine would write the program.
paragraphs.zh: 我喜欢这句话。 它是那么自信，甚至还附带了一个预算：解决问题所花的成本“不到不用 FORTRAN 时的一半”。 当年业界对这类东西有个专门的名称。 汇编器和编译器曾被称作“自动编程”。 你只需描述你想要什么，机器就会把程序写出来。

sents.zh: 汇编器和编译器曾被称作“自动编程”。

sents.zh: 你只需描述你想要什么，机器就会把程序写出来。

paragraphs.en: FORTRAN shipped in 1957, and it really did eliminate a kind of coding. Almost nobody translates formulas into machine instructions by hand anymore. Debugging survived just fine. (This month I chased a Scry bug that came down to a bookmark saved only every twelve hours, so I can confirm debugging is alive and well.)
paragraphs.zh: FORTRAN 于 1957 年发布，它确实消除了一类编码工作。 如今几乎没有人再手工把公式翻译成机器指令了。 但调试却完好地存续了下来。 （这个月我追查了一个 Scry 的 bug，最终发现根源是一个书签每十二小时才保存一次，所以我可以证明调试依然活得很好。）

sents.en: FORTRAN shipped in 1957, and it really did eliminate a kind of coding.
sents.zh: FORTRAN 于 1957 年发布，它确实消除了一类编码工作。

sents.en: Almost nobody translates formulas into machine instructions by hand anymore.
sents.zh: 如今几乎没有人再手工把公式翻译成机器指令了。

sents.en: Debugging survived just fine.
sents.zh: 但调试却完好地存续了下来。

sents.en: (This month I chased a Scry bug that came down to a bookmark saved only every twelve hours, so I can confirm debugging is alive and well.)
sents.zh: （这个月我追查了一个 Scry 的 bug，最终发现根源是一个书签每十二小时才保存一次，所以我可以证明调试依然活得很好。）

paragraphs.en: What FORTRAN actually did was take one tedious part of the job away and move the job up a level. People stopped thinking about registers and started thinking about bigger problems. Programs got cheaper to write, so everybody wanted more of them. That has happened over and over since.
paragraphs.zh: FORTRAN 实际上做的是把工作中一个繁琐的部分拿走，并将工作提升了一个层次。 人们不再考虑寄存器，而是开始思考更大的问题。 编写程序变得更便宜了，所以每个人都想要更多的程序。 从那以后，这种情况一再发生。

paragraphs.en: My favorite rung is 1981. A British company called D.J. “AI” Systems (yes, really) sold a BASIC program generator named The Last One. The name was the whole pitch. It would write all your programs for you, so it would be the last program you’d ever need to buy.
paragraphs.zh: 我最喜欢的年份是1981年。 一家名为 D.J. "AI" Systems 的英国公司（没错，真的叫这个名字）出售了一款名为 The Last One 的 BASIC 程序生成器。 这个名字本身就是全部卖点。 它会为你编写所有程序，因此它将是你需要购买的最后一个程序。

sents.zh: 我最喜欢的年份是1981年。

sents.zh: 一家名为 D.J. "AI" Systems 的英国公司（没错，真的叫这个名字）出售了一款名为 The Last One 的 BASIC 程序生成器。

paragraphs.en: Reviewers found it useful for some business programs. It was not the last one.

paragraphs.en: Here’s the pattern on every rung. Something gets automated, the people doing the work stop doing that thing by hand, and the field keeps growing anyway. GitHub counted more than 180 million developers in its 2025 report, and more than 36 million of them had joined in the previous twelve months.
paragraphs.zh: 每一级阶梯上都是同样的模式。 某些工作被自动化了，做这些工作的人不再手动去做，而这个领域依然在不断增长。 GitHub 在其 2025 年报告中统计到超过 1.8 亿开发者，其中超过 3600 万是在此前十二个月内加入的。

sents.zh: GitHub 在其 2025 年报告中统计到超过 1.8 亿开发者，其中超过 3600 万是在此前十二个月内加入的。

paragraphs.en: So I don’t think AI ends programming. I do think this rung is different in one way, and that’s speed. GitHub Copilot’s preview came out in June 2021. By 2025, 84% of developers in Stack Overflow’s survey were using AI tools or planning to. Four years, from novelty to default.
paragraphs.zh: 所以我不认为 AI 会终结编程。 我确实认为这一轮有所不同，不同之处在于速度。 GitHub Copilot 的预览版于 2021 年 6 月发布。 到 2025 年，Stack Overflow 调查中 84% 的开发者已经在使用 AI 工具或计划使用。 四年时间，从新鲜事物变成了默认选择。

sents.en: Four years, from novelty to default.
sents.zh: 四年时间，从新鲜事物变成了默认选择。

paragraphs.en: The vibes are loud right now, so let’s start with numbers. (Speaking of vibes: Andrej Karpathy coined “vibe coding” in February 2025, for the kind of coding where you “fully give in to the vibes.” Stack Overflow asked about it that year. 72% of developers said it isn’t part of their professional work, and another 5% said emphatically no. I love that they offered that option.)
paragraphs.zh: 如今舆论喧嚣，那我们就先用数字说话。 （说到舆论：Andrej Karpathy 在 2025 年 2 月创造了「氛围编程」一词，指的是那种「完全放任于氛围」的编程方式。Stack Overflow 在那一年就此做了调查。72% 的开发者表示这并非他们专业工作的一部分，另有 5% 的人斩钉截铁地说不是。 我很喜欢他们提供了这样一个选项。）

paragraphs.en: Stack Overflow’s survey is the biggest regular check-up we have, and the adoption curve in it is steep: from 70% of developers using AI tools or planning to in 2023, to 84% in 2025, when half of professional developers were using them every day.
paragraphs.zh: Stack Overflow 的调查是我们拥有的最大规模的定期体检，其中的采用曲线十分陡峭：从 2023 年 70% 的开发者正在使用或计划使用 AI 工具，到 2025 年的 84%，当时有一半的职业开发者每天都在使用这些工具。

paragraphs.en: You’d think all that use would mean developers love these tools. Nope. Favorable sentiment fell from 77% in 2023 to 60% in 2025, and only ticked back up to 62% this year. In 2025, more developers distrusted the accuracy of AI output (46%) than trusted it (33%). The top frustration, picked by 66% of them, was “AI solutions that are almost right, but not quite.”
paragraphs.zh: 你可能会以为使用这么多就意味着开发者热爱这些工具。并非如此。 好感度从 2023 年的 77% 降至 2025 年的 60%，今年才小幅回升至 62%。 在 2025 年，不信任 AI 输出准确性的开发者（46%）要多于信任它的开发者（33%）。 最令人沮丧的一点，被 66% 的开发者选中，是「AI 方案几乎正确，但又差那么一点」。

paragraphs.en: I feel seen. Almost right is an expensive kind of wrong, because you have to read every line to find the part that isn’t. (45% of them said debugging AI-generated code takes longer.)
paragraphs.zh: 我感到被理解了。 几乎正确是一种代价高昂的错误，因为你必须逐行阅读才能找出不对的那部分。 （其中45%的人表示，调试AI生成的代码耗时更长。）

paragraphs.en: Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 2023 to 2026. The 2026 survey dropped the “use or plan to” question and rewrote the trust question, so those two lines stop at 2025. About 90,000 developers answered in 2023 and more than 30,000 in 2026.

paragraphs.en: Then there’s my favorite study of the whole AI boom, mostly because it’s so rude. In early 2025, METR, a nonprofit research group, ran a proper randomized controlled trial. Sixteen experienced open-source developers worked on 246 real issues in their own repositories, projects they’d been on for years, and each issue was randomly assigned to allow AI tools or ban them.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来是整个 AI 热潮中我最喜欢的一项研究，主要是因为它太不给面子了。 2025 年初，非营利研究机构 METR 开展了一项严格的随机对照试验。 十六名经验丰富的开源开发者在他们自己的代码库中处理 246 个真实议题——这些是他们已经参与多年的项目，每个议题被随机分配为允许使用 AI 工具或禁止使用。

paragraphs.en: Before they started, the developers expected AI to cut their time by 24%. When they finished, they believed it had cut it by 20%. The clock said that with AI they took 19% longer.
paragraphs.zh: 在开始之前，开发者们预期 AI 能为他们节省 24% 的时间。 完成之后，他们相信 AI 节省了 20% 的时间。 计时结果显示，使用 AI 后他们反而多花了 19% 的时间。

paragraphs.en: And METR tried to run it again. A bigger study started in August 2025, with 57 developers and more than 800 tasks, and in February 2026 METR said the data was too unreliable to lean on. Mostly that was because developers kept declining to take part, since they “do not wish to work without AI.” The early numbers hinted at an 18% speedup for the returning developers (with a range wide enough to include no speedup at all).
paragraphs.zh: 而 METR 试图再次进行这项研究。 一项更大规模的研究于 2025 年 8 月启动，涉及 57 名开发者和 800 多项任务，而到 2026 年 2 月，METR 表示数据太不可靠，不足以作为依据。 主要原因在于开发者不断拒绝参与，因为他们“不愿在没有 AI 的情况下工作”。早期数字暗示，回归的开发者获得了 18% 的提速（但置信区间宽到足以包含完全没有提速的情况）。

paragraphs.en: What I take from METR is narrower than any headline, and more useful: how fast you feel is not a measurement. If you want to know whether AI makes your team faster, measure it the way you’d measure anything else.

paragraphs.en: METR’s other big project tracks how long a task an AI agent can finish on its own. They time human experts on a suite of software tasks, then find the task length where an agent succeeds half the time. In 2019, GPT-2 managed tasks that take a person about three seconds. GPT-4 got to about four minutes in 2023. Claude 3.7 Sonnet reached an hour in February 2025, and Claude Opus 4.6 reached about twelve hours a year later.
paragraphs.zh: METR 的另一个大型项目追踪 AI 智能体能独立完成的任务时长。 他们对人类专家完成一组软件任务的时间进行计时，然后找出智能体成功率为一半的任务时长。 2019 年，GPT-2 能完成人类大约需要三秒钟的任务。 2023 年，GPT-4 达到了大约四分钟。 Claude 3.7 Sonnet 在 2025 年 2 月达到了一小时，而 Claude Opus 4.6 在一年后达到了约十二小时。

METR says anything above 16 hours is unreliable with its current tasks, so Claude Mythos Preview’s 17-hour measurement in May isn’t on the line. The dashed part extends the six-month doubling. It’s a trend, not a promise.

paragraphs.en: Now, a log-scale chart with a dashed line on the end is how a lot of bad predictions start, so let me be careful. “Half the time” is doing a lot of work in that definition. Benchmark tasks are cleaner than your codebase. And METR stopped updating that page in September. But if the line keeps going even roughly, agents will handle a month of human work, half the time, around 2028. That’s where my 2031 Tuesday comes from. I didn’t pull it out of thin air. paragraphs.en: The companies building these things are already living a version of it. Google said in October 2024 that more than a quarter of its new code was generated by AI, and “well over 30%” six months later. In March 2025, Anthropic’s Dario Amodei predicted AI would be writing 90% of code within three to six months. That was too soon. But by May 2026, Anthropic said more than 80% of the code merged into its own codebase was written by Claude.
paragraphs.zh: 构建这些产品的公司已经生活在其中一种版本之中。 谷歌在 2024 年 10 月表示，其超过四分之一的新代码由 AI 生成，六个月后这一比例达到了“远超 30%”。 2025 年 3 月，Anthropic 的 Dario Amodei 预测 AI 将在三到六个月内编写 90% 的代码。这个预测来得太早了。 但到 2026 年 5 月，Anthropic 表示，合入其自身代码库的代码中有超过 80% 是由 Claude 编写的。

paragraphs.en: Make one step of a process faster and the work piles up in front of the next slowest step. Anyone who has worked a kitchen on a Saturday night knows this: speed up the grill and the plates start waiting at the pass.
paragraphs.zh: 让流程中的某一步变快，工作就会堆积在下一个最慢的步骤前面。 任何在周六晚上在后厨干过的人都知道这一点：加快烤炉的速度，餐盘就会开始在出菜口排队等候。

paragraphs.en: That’s what’s happening to software teams. In 2025, Faros AI looked at telemetry from more than 10,000 developers on 1,255 teams. Developers on teams with high AI adoption finished 21% more tasks and merged 98% more pull requests, and their review time went up 91%.
paragraphs.zh: 这正是软件团队正在经历的事情。 2025 年，Faros AI 分析了来自 1,255 个团队、超过 10,000 名开发者的遥测数据。 高 AI 采用率团队的开发者完成了多 21% 的任务，合并了多 98% 的拉取请求，而他们的评审时间上升了 91%。

paragraphs.en: Faros ran it again in 2026 with 22,000 developers. Task completion per developer was up 34%, which sounds great until you read the rest. Median review time had grown five times. 31% more pull requests were merging without any review at all, and the ratio of incidents to pull requests had more than tripled.
paragraphs.zh: Faros 在 2026 年用 22,000 名开发者再次进行了这项研究。 每位开发者的任务完成率提升了 34%，这听起来很不错，直到你读完其余的内容。 中位数评审时间增长到了原来的五倍。31% 的更多拉取请求在完全没有评审的情况下被合并，而且事故与拉取请求的比例增长了两倍以上。

paragraphs.en: The code got cheaper, the reading got more expensive, and some teams quietly stopped reading. That matters because the code isn’t always good. Veracode tested more than 100 language models on 80 coding tasks in 2025, and 45% of the results had a security flaw. GitClear found that copy-pasted lines went from 8.3% of changed code in 2021 to 12.3% in 2024, while moved code, the kind you get from refactoring, fell from about a quarter to under 10%.
paragraphs.zh: 代码变得更便宜了，阅读却变得更昂贵了，一些团队悄悄停止了阅读。 这一点很重要，因为代码并不总是好的。 Veracode 在 2025 年对 100 多个语言模型进行了 80 项编码任务的测试，其中 45% 的结果存在安全缺陷。 GitClear 发现，复制粘贴的代码行从 2021 年占变更代码的 8.3% 上升到 2024 年的 12.3%，而移动代码（即通过重构得到的代码）的比例则从大约四分之一降至 10% 以下。

paragraphs.en: Fred Brooks saw a version of this coming in 1986. In “No Silver Bullet” he split the difficulties of software into two piles, borrowing Aristotle’s words: essence and accidents. The accidents are the trouble our tools cause us, like syntax, boilerplate and fighting the build. The essence is what he called “the specification, design, and testing of this conceptual construct,” which is a fancy way of saying: working out what the thing should do. AI is getting very good at the accidents. The essence is the refund question from 2:13 a.m., and it’s still on your desk.
paragraphs.zh: 弗雷德·布鲁克斯早在1986年就预见了这一问题的一种版本。 在《没有银弹》中，他借亚里士多德之词，将软件的困难分为两类：本质与偶然。 偶然是我们的工具给我们带来的麻烦，比如语法、样板代码以及与构建系统搏斗。 本质则是他所说的「这一概念性构造的规格说明、设计与测试」，说得通俗点就是：搞清楚这个东西到底应该做什么。 AI 在偶然层面的表现已经非常出色。 本质则是凌晨2:13那个退款问题，它仍然躺在你的桌上。

paragraphs.en: The Stanford authors are careful to call their findings descriptive, not causal, and plenty else has happened since 2022. Interest rates went up, and a lot of companies had hired too many people during the pandemic (Indeed’s index peaked at more than twice its 2020 level in early 2022). But the pattern lines up uncomfortably well with what agents are good at: the small, well-defined ticket we used to give the new person on the team.
paragraphs.zh: 斯坦福大学的作者们谨慎地称他们的发现是描述性的，而非因果性的，况且自2022年以来还发生了许多其他事情。 利率上升，许多公司在疫情期间招聘了过多的员工（Indeed的指数在2022年初达到峰值，是其2020年水平的两倍多）。 但这种模式与智能体所擅长的内容吻合得令人不安：那些我们过去交给团队新人的小巧、定义明确的工作单。

paragraphs.en: Senior engineers get made on the job, mostly by being juniors on real teams: doing the boring tickets, breaking production once, and having someone kind explain why. paragraphs.en: Teams get smaller, and there are a lot more of them. According to Y Combinator’s Jared Friedman, a quarter of the Winter 2025 batch had codebases that were about 95% AI-generated. In February, Block cut about 4,000 jobs, and Jack Dorsey pointed to AI tools and “smaller and flatter teams.” I could be wrong here, but I still don’t think that adds up to fewer software jobs overall, and neither does the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, which projects 10% growth for software developers, QA analysts and testers from 2025 to 2035.
paragraphs.zh: 团队规模变得更小，而团队数量却多得多。 根据 Y Combinator 的 Jared Friedman 的说法，2025 年冬季批次中有四分之一的代码库约 95% 由 AI 生成。 今年二月，Block 裁减了约 4,000 个职位，Jack Dorsey 指出了 AI 工具以及「更小、更扁平的团队」。我在这点上可能有误，但我仍然不认为这意味着软件行业的工作岗位整体会减少，美国劳工统计局也不这么认为，该机构预计 2025 年至 2035 年间软件开发人员、QA 分析师和测试人员的岗位将增长 10%。

paragraphs.en: When something gets cheaper, we tend to want more of it. Economists call this the Jevons paradox, after William Stanley Jevons, who argued in 1865 that more efficient steam engines would make Britain burn more coal. Software that took a team a quarter will take one person a week, and a lot of problems nobody could afford to solve will suddenly be worth solving.
paragraphs.zh: 当某样东西变得更便宜时，我们往往会想要更多。 经济学家称之为杰文斯悖论，得名于威廉·斯坦利·杰文斯，他在1865年论证，效率更高的蒸汽机会使英国燃烧更多的煤炭。 过去需要一个团队一个季度才能完成的软件，如今一个人一周就能完成，许多过去没人负担得起去解决的问题，将突然变得值得解决。

paragraphs.en: The spec and the tests become the source. Today we treat the code as the thing we own and the spec as the document nobody reads. I think that flips. The spec and the tests become what you review and argue about, and the code becomes more like a compiler’s output: you can open it and inspect it, but you rarely edit it by hand. (Yes, that’s the 1954 promise again. Maybe this time it sticks.)

paragraphs.en: Software for an audience of one. My nightly agent builds things nobody asked for, including me, and some of them are delightful. When a working tool costs an evening instead of a quarter, people will make software the way they make spreadsheets today: for one problem and one person, thrown away when it’s done.
paragraphs.zh: 为一个人打造的软件。 我的夜间智能体会构建一些没人要求的东西，包括我自己要求过的，其中有些还颇为令人愉悦。 当一个可用的工具只需一个晚上而不是一个季度就能做出来时，人们会像今天制作电子表格那样制作软件：为解决一个问题、服务一个人而生，用完即弃。

paragraphs.en: Reading code becomes a career. We have whole careers built around writing code and almost none built around reading it. I expect that to change, with something like “verification engineer” on job boards and much better tooling that shows a reviewer the recording, the risky lines and the tests the agent didn’t write. The Faros numbers say we need it now, never mind in 2031.

paragraphs.en: I think AI does the same thing, faster and messier. The developer of 2031 spends the day deciding what should exist, explaining it clearly enough that a machine can build it, and checking that what came back is right. That was always the hard part. We just had less time for it because we were busy typing.
paragraphs.zh: 我认为 AI 做的是同一件事，只是更快、也更混乱。 2031 年的开发者一整天都在决定什么应该被创造出来，把它解释得足够清楚以便机器能够构建它，并检查返回的结果是否正确。 这一直都是最难的部分。 只是我们以前时间更少，因为忙着敲键盘。
